questions.question:

__
 
• The most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in "**The ****child felt down__**** from a great height**." is child fell down. 
 
• The child fell down from a great height.
 
• Therefore **option 3 **is the correct option.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**Select the correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select ‘No substitution’.**

He is __faster than smarter__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'more fast than smart'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Two **different prepositions** are used to describe two **different adjectives**. However, **a single preposition** is used if two adjectives agree with the same preposition.
 
• Examples:
 
 
• I am slower and bigger than you. (correct)
 
• I am smaller than but superior to you. (correct)
 
 
 
• Similarly, in this context, **'more fast than smart'** should be used.

Hence, the corrected sentence is: ***He is more fast than smart***.

questions.question:

Vicky and Deepa (tries their level best) to run from the ritual.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**try their level best**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The most appropriate substitution for the bracketed word segment '**(tries their level best)**' is '**try their level best**' .
 
• **Subject-verb agreement rule**- Singular nouns go with singular verbs while plural nouns go with plural verbs and in this case "Vicky and Deepa" together made the subject plural so plural form of verb will be used i.e** try their level best **.
 
 
• E.g. *We say, She **looks **very pretty and not She **look **very pretty.*
 
• Hence, the **most appropriate** substitute is '**try their level best**'.

questions.question:
**Select the option that can substitute the bracketed word segment correctly and complete the following sentence meaningfully.**

Lots of kids (was visualised) crossing the road when the bus arrived.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'were seen'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's break down the sentence and analyze it: *"Lots of kids (**was visualized**) crossing the road when the bus arrived."*
 
• In this sentence, the subject is **"lots of kids,"** which is** a plural noun** because it refers to multiple children. Therefore, the **verb that follows should also be plural to agree with the subject.**
 
• The verb in the bracketed segment,** "was visualized," **is in **the past tense and singular form, **which does not agree with **the plural subject "lots of kids."**
 
• The correct** verb form to use with a plural subject is "were." **Therefore, the corrected sentence would be:* "Lots of kids (**were seen**) crossing the road when the bus arrived."*
 
• Here, **"were seen"** is the correct** past tense plural form of the verb "to see," **which **agrees with the plural subject "lots of kids."**
 
• So, the grammatical reason for choosing **"were seen"** is that it correctly matches **the subject's plurality,** making the sentence grammatically accurate.

questions.question:

No sooner had she finished her breakfast __that she had received__ a phone call from her boss, informing her that she needed to come to work immediately
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

**__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, the correct conjunction to use after **"No sooner" is "than" and not "that".**
 
• The phrase** "No sooner... than" **is a **correlative conjunction used to show that one thing happens immediately after another.**
 
 
• **No sooner had I started mowing the lawn, than it started raining**​
 
• **No sooner had I spoken than he appeared**
 
 

Therefore, the correct sentence is: **"No sooner had she finished her breakfast than she received a phone call from her boss, informing her that she needed to come to work immediately."**

questions.question:

The cat climbed a tree and __perched__ itself on a branch.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• This is the appropriate action for a cat that has climbed a tree.
 
• The term "**perched**" is contextually correct, as it follows logically after mentioning that the cat climbed a tree, indicating it has settled on a branch.
 
• Other options such as "**parched**," "**perked**", and "**perished**" do not fit the context of the sentence.
 
• "**Parched**" refers to being dried out with heat, "**perked**" suggests becoming more cheerful or lively, and "**perished**" means dying, which is not relevant to the action of sitting or settling on a branch.
 
• The sentence is grammatically correct with the use of "**perched itself on a branch**" as it clearly communicates what the cat did after climbing the tree.

Therefore, the correct answer is **No substitution required**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Parched:** (सूखा) This option suggests a state of being dry or thirsty, which would not logically follow the verb "climbed" in the context of a cat climbing a tree.
 
• **Perked:** (उत्साहित) This could imply a sudden improvement in mood or condition, which is not what is described by the action of sitting on a branch after climbing.
 
• **Perished:**(मारे गए) This option indicates death, which is entirely unrelated to the action described in the sentence and would significantly change its meaning in an incorrect way.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution’.

I like to read books, but my brother prefers __to watching__ movies.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2. to watch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The underlined segment **"to watching"** is grammatically **incorrect **in this context.
 
• The correct construction uses "to" followed by the base form of the verb (infinitive form), not the gerund (verb-ing form).
 
• prefer + infinitive (to + base form of the verb).
 
 
• Example: I prefer to read.
 
 
 
• **"To watch"** is the **correct **form, as it maintains parallelism with the first part of the sentence ("I like to read").
 
• The phrase should smoothly follow the verb "**prefers**," which is typically followed by "**to**" and the base form of a verb to indicate preference.

Therefore, the correct sentence is- *I like to read books, but my brother prefers **to watch__** movies. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **__Confusion Points__**

 
• prefer + noun + to + noun.
 
 
• **Example:** I prefer tea to coffee.
 
 
 
• prefer + gerund (verb+ing) + to + gerund.
 
 
• **Example:** I prefer reading to watching TV.
 
 
 
• **prefer + infinitive (to + base form of the verb).**
 
 
• **Example:** I prefer to read.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the structure is meant to express a preference for an activity (watching movies) over another (reading books).
 
• Since the sentence starts with "I like to read books," we should maintain a parallel structure for the second part of the sentence related to the brother's preference.

Therefore, the correct construction is "prefers to watch," not "prefer to watching".

__
 
• **"Go hand in hand" **is **an idiomatic expression** that means** two things are closely related or work together very well**, which aligns with the idea that politics and money are interconnected in this country.
 
• This phrase effectively conveys the notion that the two concepts described (politics and money) are interdependent or commonly found together, which is the intended meaning in the sentence.

Therefore, the best fit for substitution is- Politics and money ***go hand in together__ ***in this country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Go arm in arm** (Option 1) and **go holding hands** (Option 2) are phrases that can denote closeness or partnership but are more often used to describe physical closeness between people rather than metaphorical or conceptual relationships like that between politics and money.

questions.question:

Harry is the one sitting __on__ the corner.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4. i.e. **'in'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"sitting on the corner" is** usually used for external settings, such as sitting on the corner of a street.
 
• **"In the corner" **is the most appropriate prepositional phrase for describing someone's location within an internal, enclosed space, like a room or an area bounded by walls.
 
• Hence, substituting "sitting on the corner" with "sitting in the corner" improves the clarity and preciseness of the original sentence’s intended meaning.

Therefore, the complete correct is *"Harry is the one sitting **in__ **the corner."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Upon:** This preposition typically denotes being on top of or being in contact with a surface.
 
• **Onto:** Suggests movement from one place to another, emphasizing the action of moving to a position rather than being stationary.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The dance performance __was more beautifuler__ than I expected.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**was more beautiful**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **most appropriate** answer according to the **Degree rules** of the English language is '**was more beautiful**'.
 
• The word '**beautifuler**' does not exist in the English language.
 
• According to the Degree rule__, '***An adjective in comparative degree is usually followed by 'than'***.
 
• The forms of degree for the adjective beautiful will be as follows:
 
 
• **Positive Degree**- Beautiful
 
• **Comparative Degree**- More beautiful
 
• **Superlative Degree**- Most beautiful.
 
 
 
• Hence, considering the above-mentioned points, the correct answer is '**was more beautiful**'.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

The Taj Mahal is one of the __much__ popular seven wonders of the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**most**'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate substitute for the underlined part is '**most**'.
 
• Explanation: In the **given sentence**, the** phrase "much popular" is grammatically incorrect.** The correct phrase should be** "most popular." **When comparing the popularity of the **Taj Mahal with the other wonders of the world,** **the superlative form "most" **should be used to indicate that it is the highest in popularity among them.
 
• ***Here's the corrected sentence:**__ "The Taj Mahal is one of the **most** popular seven wonders of the world." *
 
• **Option 4**, "**most**," is the correct answer because it replaces "**much**" with the appropriate** superlative form,** making the sentence grammatically correct.
 
• **Options 2 and 3, "more" and "much more,"** respectively, are incorrect because they do not convey the superlative comparison required in this context. Instead, they suggest a comparative degree, which is not suitable for comparing the Taj Mahal's popularity with the other wonders of the world.
